thread.title: Behind Lee Beebe, Indiana able to overcome injuries and inconsistency to beat Northwestern - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Behind Lee Beebe, Indiana able to overcome injuries and inconsistency to beat Northwestern - NewsBreak

author: Ben Kruer
title: Behind Lee Beebe, Indiana able to overcome injuries and inconsistency to beat Northwestern - NewsBreak
text:
By Ben Kruer ,
21 hours ago
Indiana's Lee Beebe Jr. (29) runs during the Indiana versus Northwestern football game at Memorial Stadium on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. As Curt Cignetti left the field after the first half, he told Fox’s Alexa Landestoy that it had been a “weird” game so far. He wasn’t wrong.
Indiana led 12-0 (weird enough score on its own) but had nearly 200 more yards than Northwestern, and really, it felt like more. The offense and defense statistically whooped the Wildcats but a 12-point lead was all the Hoosiers had to show for it.
Part of it was the penalties that Indiana racked up throughout the game. The Hoosiers had four for 35 yards in the first half, and eight for 60 yards on the game. There were the stalled drives–one where Indiana ended up settling for a field goal and another where Indiana turned it over on downs.
There was the injury to Turbo Richard which knocked him out of the game. A potentially devastating blow to an already thin running back room. Josh Hoover had a poor first quarter, but followed it up with a dazzling second quarter. Indiana’s offense was doing a Jekyll-and-Hyde routine all half and again, Indiana found itself winning by less than it should have.
Because of the defense’s early dominance, this inconsistency didn’t seem to matter all that much. But when the second half turned into an Aidan Chiles showcase, Indiana needed its offense to rise to the occasion in a way that it had not yet needed to this season. It was an early test for an Indiana team with high expectations.
An up-and-down showing can work against teams like North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky, but not Northwestern. The Northwesterns of the college football world demand a higher standard.
Indiana’s offense still found a way to gut out a win, and it was on the back of Lee Beebe .
“Boy, we really needed him and he carried the load,” Cignetti said.
Those who may have thought Richard’s injury may lead to Hoover throwing the ball more clearly misunderstood the core principles of Indiana’s offensive creed. This is a team that loves to run the football, and nothing will stop them from doing so.
Beebe had his best game as a Hoosier. After missing most of the 2025 season with a knee injury, Beebe exploded against Northwestern for 203 yards on 24 attempts. When Chiles scored a touchdown to make the score 15-13 in favor of the Hoosiers, it was Beebe who responded for Indiana.
“I’m really proud of [Beebe] and the way he stepped up tonight with [Richard] going down,” Hoover said. “He had a lot of carries, but he did a great job.”
On the next drive, Beebe exploded for a 39 yard gain. He then punched it in for Indiana to extend their lead to nine–making it a two possession game.
Then Chiles did it again. He willed Northwestern down the field and on a third-and-goal from the 13-yard line, he scrambled from the pocket, making Hoosier defenders miss on his way to another touchdown to shrink Northwestern’s deficit back to two.
In this game of tit-for-tat, it was Beebe’s turn. On the first play of the next drive, Beebe skirted around the left side of the line for a 70 yard gain. He was aided by an excellent block by Shazz Preston , but Beebe’s stiff arm to cap off the play was just as pretty.
“I just knew to stay patient and was like, ‘This is going to pop,’” Beebe said.
Indiana then struggled to get into the endzone, and again, it was Beebe who was partially responsible. This time, he acted as a decoy for Hoover, who faked the handoff to Beebe and kept it himself to walk into the endzone untouched.
It was also Beebe who sealed the game for Indiana. After the Hoosiers recovered the onside kick, they needed just one first down to eke out the win. On a third-and-one, Indiana gave it to Beebe. He should have been stuffed in the backfield as his own offensive lineman was shoved into him, but as was the case all night, Beebe found a way. He bounced it to the outside, broke a tackle, and secured the first down–and the victory–for Indiana.
“I just know I need to step up and be there for the team, and I was able to do that,” Beebe said.
No other running back entered the game until Indiana entered the victory formation. And even then, Beebe was still on the field. Indiana probably doesn’t win this game if Beebe doesn’t have the best game of his life. There’s a lot of problems that Indiana could fix from this game–Beebe’s performance is not one of them.
“He’s got as much heart as anybody that’s been in this program the last three years,” Cignetti said.
